title: Knowing the Truth
note: This means knowing birth, release and their causes as they are, without error or doubt. It too comes from holding to the one who has no attachment, so it follows renunciation.

couplets.plain: A wretched birth comes from the delusion that takes what isn’t real for what is.
couplets.pm: A birth without joy comes from false understanding: trusting books that deny rebirth, the fruit of deeds and god as true books, or taking a post for a man or a shell for silver. All four kinds of birth, in hell, as beasts, as humans and as gods, are only suffering. Delusion is the first cause of birth.

links.quote: the delusion that takes what isn’t real for what is
links.reason: Blames a wretched birth on one error, taking what isn’t real for what is.

couplets.plain: For those who have left delusion behind and see without stain, darkness goes and joy comes.
couplets.pm: For those free of delusion who have true knowledge, that knowledge removes birth and gives release. The darkness is hell, which stands for birth, its cause. Release is joy beyond compare, and seeing without stain means knowing the one absolute reality.

links.reason: Shows what its removal yields: those rid of it get joy in place of darkness.
Credits stainless seeing with bringing joy to the one who has it.

couplets.plain: For those who have left doubt behind and see clearly, heaven is nearer than the earth.
couplets.pm: For those free of doubt who know the truth, the world of release they are to reach is nearer than the earth they stand on. Doubt is wavering over whether rebirth, the fruit of deeds and god exist, like “mirage or water, rope or snake”. Those ripe in yoga clear it by experience, and their old worldly sense fades.

links.quote: heaven is nearer than the earth
links.reason: Puts heaven nearer than earth for those whose doubts have ended.

couplets.plain: Even if you have mastered the awareness of the five senses, there is no gain in it without knowledge of the truth.
couplets.pm: The fivefold awareness is the mind, five because of the senses it runs to. Even when it leaves them, comes under control and stays fixed in concentration, there is no gain for those who don’t know the truth, because it can’t give release. That fixed state is hard to reach, and still it isn’t enough.
couplets.note: ஐயுணர்வு can mean simply the five senses. He reads it as the mind held still in concentration.

links.quote: no gain in it without knowledge of the truth
links.reason: Counts even mastery of the senses as no gain without knowledge of the truth.

couplets.plain: Whatever a thing may be, and however it may seem, understanding is seeing the reality in it.
couplets.pm: Whatever a thing appears to be, true knowledge doesn’t stop there. It removes what the world imagines and sees the truth within. A ruler’s caste, family, looks and titles are all imagined. See him as a gathering of elements, from earth up to the soul, resolve each into its cause, and you reach what is left at the end. All things are known this way.

links.quote: understanding is seeing the reality in it
links.reason: Names the work of understanding as finding the true in every thing, whatever form it takes.

couplets.plain: Those who learn here and see the truth will reach the path that doesn’t come back here.
couplets.pm: Those who in this human birth hear the teaching from an experienced teacher and so know the truth reach the path of no return to this birth, the path to release. “Learn” means hearing many teachers many times, and “here” shows how hard a human birth is to get. There are three means of knowing the truth: hearing, reflection and meditation. This is the first.

links.quote: Those who learn here and see the truth
links.reason: Joins learning to insight and rewards the pair with a path that doesn’t come back.

links.quote: the path that doesn’t come back here

couplets.plain: If your mind examines and surely knows what truly is, you need not think of being born again.
couplets.pm: If your mind tests the teaching it has heard by the means of knowledge and by reason, examines it clearly and so knows the first reality, you need not think there is any birth for you again. This is the second means, reflection.

links.quote: you need not think of being born again
links.reason: Relieves the one who has reasoned their way to what truly is of all thought of another birth.

couplets.plain: To end the folly called birth and see the pure reality called excellence: that is understanding.
couplets.pm: True knowledge is seeing the pure reality that leads to release, so that delusion, first cause of birth, is destroyed. Release is called excellence as the best of all things. This reality is eternal, pure and changeless. To see it is to meditate without a break until the soul is one with it, since at death the soul becomes what it dwells on. This is the third means.

links.quote: see the pure reality called excellence
links.reason: Gives understanding its aim: to see the pure reality called excellence.
Birth itself is the folly here, and ending it is what understanding aims at.

couplets.plain: If you know what to rest on and live so that attachment dies, the ills that would come to you are destroyed and won’t come.
couplets.pm: If you know the pure reality that all things rest on and live so that both attachments end, the sufferings due to reach you can’t reach you. Living here means the eight limbs of yoga. Those sufferings are the stored fruit of deeds from endless births, and they vanish before wisdom and yoga like darkness before a lamp. Even the fruit of good deeds counts as ills.

links.reason: Treats living so that attachment dies as what sends future ills away.

links.quote: If you know what to rest on
links.reason: Knowing what to rest on is this insight, and it comes before the living.

couplets.plain: When even the names of these three, desire, anger and delusion, are gone, pain is gone.
couplets.pm: For those ripe in wisdom and yoga, even the names of these three faults, desire, hatred and delusion, perish, so the fruits of deeds no longer arise. Before unbroken wisdom and yoga they are like cotton before a forest fire. With the cause gone, no new deeds are done and no new suffering comes. Only this body and the deeds that brought it remain.

links.reason: Heads the three whose going takes pain along with it.
Stands between desire and delusion among the three whose names must go for pain to go.

ideaLinks.quote: A wretched birth comes from the delusion
ideaLinks.reason: Taking what isn’t real for what is brings a wretched birth.

ideaLinks.quote: reach the path that doesn’t come back here
ideaLinks.reason: Whoever has seen the truth reaches the path that doesn’t come back here.
